acceptance: On Polars 2.0.0 and on 1.44.2, benchbox run --platform polars-df at SF 0.01 completes for tpch, tpcds, ssb and clickbench with zero failed queries and the expected query count per benchmark (no zero-query runs)
python -m benchbox.core.equivalence.cross_surface --benchmark <b> reports no divergences beyond cross_surface_baseline.yaml for all four benchmarks on both 2.0.0 and 1.44.2
cast_date uses an API available from Polars 1.0.0 onwards, and a unit test covers a String input
The PR body lists every 2.0 removal or default change checked against BenchBox code with file:line, and every added deterministic sort per query
uv.lock, the pyproject polars floor and the main checkout's environment are unchanged; existing CI is green

description:
Polars 2.0.0 (released 2026-10-06) is a breaking release, and BenchBox's polars-df surface has only been exercised on 1.x (uv.lock 1.44.2, floor polars>=1.35.2). Make TPC-H, TPC-DS, SSB and ClickBench run and match their SQL reference on 2.0.0 while still passing on 1.44.2.

Known 2.0 changes that affect us (Polars 2 upgrade guide, docs.pola.rs/releases/upgrade/2/):
- String-to-temporal cast via cast(pl.Date) is rejected; use str.to_date(). This breaks polars_df.py cast_date (column.cast(pl.Date)).
- collect() defaults to the streaming engine, which does not guarantee row order for joins, group_by or unpivot.
- profile() removed; read_csv n_threads, batch_size, sample_size and rechunk removed; horizontal concat requires equal heights; Int+UInt64 supertype becomes Int128; decimal round, ceil and floor widen precision.
- Out-of-core spilling is on by default, at 80% of RAM.

Guardrails:
- Work in a separate git worktree with its own virtual environment. Never install Polars 2.0 into the main checkout's environment, and do not change uv.lock or the pyproject polars floor in this item.
- One code path for every version: no `if pl.__version__ ...` branches. Every replacement API must exist in every version the matrix may measure, down to 1.0.0; record that check per API in the PR body.
- Only change query semantics where a result is order-dependent and needs a deterministic sort; such a sort applies to every version and must be listed per query in the PR body.
- Read the full upgrade guide and the deprecation-removal table before editing; record any other call sites found.
